scope: Prepared service publication for resolved GetUp graphs and an optional companion melee frame; exact detached source-artifact retention

cases.expected: Preparation changes no authority; commit publishes graph, selected resource, clock, raw byte, action and one verified CRT transition together. A competing or consumed token cannot publish. Contact action identity remains independently pending.

Already resolved ready/start/complete/destruct candidates publish graph references and process action consistently. Completed requests retain cache/NI references; cleanup retains allocation frontier and roundtrips schema73.
Retained request/resource/NI bindings cannot be retargeted; removed identities cannot be reused; allocation frontier cannot rewind.
RNG mutation, raw-byte ABA, clock advance, restore and service replacement invalidate the transaction before any write.

A matching transferred melee frame and GetUp graph publish at one actor clock; standalone competing frame becomes stale. Missing, foreign, stale and mismatched-clock frames fail without partial publication.
An owned body reaction or strike must retain its process action in the resolved candidate; actor clock cannot rewind. This boundary does not itself retire or cancel owners.
Low-process cleanup permits an empty graph/frontier with absent process byte/action/resource. It rejects newly claimed active-process authority.
Malformed or stale CRT transitions, unsupported byte, nonfinite clock, foreign actor resource and pending IO state reject without writes.

A detached source clones the exact retained KF holder without a backend lookup or cache lease. After last info release, a new acquisition gets replacement bytes while the old source still samples the old pose.

allocation_probe.expected: All reached single-allocation failures during candidate preparation leave the full service snapshot unchanged; insert, replace, erase, companion publication and stale/consumed rejection perform no allocations. A malloc denial control verifies interposition.
allocation_probe.boundary: Standalone normal engine-library host, glibc malloc/calloc/realloc injection, headless fixtures. Some FormKey allocation failures become validation exceptions.
